International Cheese Federation Industry News
This section of the International Cheese Federation website presents a collection of industry news articles, primarily authored by Yuri Lee. The articles cover recent market trends, price fluctuations for cheese (e.g., Cheddar) and milk (Class III/IV), the impact of dairy herd size, export demand, and the implications of various tariffs (Mexico, China, EU) and federal dairy safety-net programs. The content provides timely insights into economic and policy developments affecting cheesemakers and the broader dairy industry.

Cheddar closes June at a three-year high 

 

Block and barrel cheddar closed June at prices not seen since late 2016, with firmer export demand doing a lot of the work. What that does and doesn’t mean for your milk check.

A smaller herd and a firmer price 

 

Milk prices have firmed through the spring as the national dairy herd keeps shrinking. For cheesemakers on contract pricing, this is the moment to look at renewal math.

One tariff line opens as another closes

What the spring flush means for supply this year 

 

April’s federal price data confirms a modest spring flush this year, not the flood some producers braced for. Here’s what that steadier surge means for your supply planning.

The margin picture, through February
